description: PipelineRunner (plan §12.3, §20): the only code that moves a job between states. run(job) loads the job's record; its steps are the record's plan, or JobPlanner.initial(request) when it has none (stored as the plan). Steps already done (JobPlanner.done: the leading ones by seq that succeeded or were skipped, or failed after the commit) are not run again, and the log file keeps what an earlier run wrote. The configuration is read once, when the job starts (owner, 2026-10-11): every step of the run sees that snapshot, even when it changes while the job runs. The job is submitted to its queue. For each step from the first one not done: the job's progress names the step (step, stepIndex, stepCount, fraction of the job so far, operation job.op.starting), the runner asks the Scheduler for the step's resources (while it waits, the job is waitingForResources or blocked, with blockedBy), the job becomes running, the step runs on a worker with a StepContext (the job's snapshot with every earlier step's output, its cancellation token, progress, log, decisions, tools, …), then the lease goes back, the step's record is stored and stepFinished is published. A Release step also gives back the job's drives and moves it to the processing queue. A step's report may append steps (Plan decides the rest of the list), skip (the step is skipped and the job goes on), fail (with its error), or carry what the outcome needs (read errors, quarantine, a MakeMKV notice, a reason to skip the whole job, whether a failure counts). A reason to skip the whole job ends it: no step after that one runs. A step's checkpoint (ICheckpointer.save, plan §12.2) is stored with its running row and kept on the row it finishes with; the step's next attempt in the job (a run after a restart or a retry) gets the latest one of its kind as ICheckpointer.saved. A step's read errors are stored with its output (StepOutput.readErrors), so a job resumed after it still ends with them. A report's plan (Plan's: mode, profile, library) is stored as the job's plan with the steps it appends, and its mode as the job's mode. A job that ends while it still holds its drive (it stopped before its Release step: failed, skipped or cancelled) runs the Release step once more, unstored, with its outcome as the context's finishing (owner, 2026-10-18): its log lines are kept; a job that gave its drive back, or never held one, doesn't. The runner stops at the first failed step, unless the step comes after the commit (JobOutcome.afterCommit): those failures are recorded and the job goes on. Progress is coalesced to one jobChanged per 100 ms per job (the last value of a step goes out when it ends). Log lines go out as jobLog events at once and are written to jobs/<id>/log.jsonl ({t, severity, code, params}) when each step ends, and while one runs: a step's first line at once, later ones at most every 2 s, so a crash in a long step keeps them; a write that fails then is left to the next. Seal and keepApart's lines wait for the step's end: they copy the file. A decision makes the job awaitingDecision until decide(job, answer) gives one of the answers (job.notAwaitingDecision when it isn't waiting for one; server.badRequest for another answer). cancel(job) cancels the job's token: a waiting request or a decision ends at once, a running step sees it; the job ends cancelled, and no step starts after a cancel (a step that finishes anyway is the last). A job is live (cancel reaches it) from the moment run is called, before its record is loaded. At the end JobOutcome.decide gives the outcome, the record is finished, the Scheduler forgets the job and jobFinished is published. The harness uses a real executor, Scheduler and EventBus, a manual clock at 2026-10-02T20:00:00.000Z, an in-memory store and file system, data folder /data, and fake steps that do what 'steps' says; jobs get ids in the order given (00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000001, …). Fake step behaviour: drive (the job's driveId as its drive), resources {drives, acquisition, libraryWrites, cpu, io}, output (its data; default {}), echo <kind> (its data is that earlier step's), append [kinds], skipped, fail {code, params}, readErrors, quarantined, notice (keyExpired, evaluationNotStarted, versionTooOld, libreDriveRequired), skipJob {code, params}, affectsOutcome, progress [[fraction, code], …] (reported one after another), log [codes], ask {id, question, answers} (its data is {answer}), checkpoint (saved with ICheckpointer.save before the step ends), saved (true: its data is {saved: ICheckpointer.saved}), context (true: its data is {startedAt: the snapshot's startedAt or null, appVersion: the context's, message: the context's renderer's text for job.cancelled; the harness's environment gives appVersion "test"}), reserve {volume, path, need, free} (SpaceReservations.reserve through the runner and the Scheduler; a failure fails the step), plan {mode, profileId, libraryId} (the report's plan), gate <name> (waits until 'open', or fails with job.cancelled when cancelled), ignoresCancel (its gate waits for 'open' even when the job is cancelled), config <key> (its data is {key: that member of the context's configuration document}). Run with a finishing outcome (the Release at the end), a step only logs its 'log' codes, and the harness records '<outcome> <error code>'. Ops: run <job>; open <gate>; cancel <job>; decide {job, answer, expectError}; advance <ms>; library {id, online} (Scheduler.setLibraryOffline with library.offline {library: id}); config <document> (what the configuration source gives from then on). Given: config (the configuration document; default {}), jobs [{name, kind (videoDisc), title (its name), driveId, automatic, queue (acquisition), plan (none: the planner's), done [{kind, output, state}] (stored steps, by seq; state succeeded unless given), log [codes] (lines already in jobs/<id>/log.jsonl, as an earlier run or recovery left them)}], steps {kind: behaviour} (a kind not listed just succeeds). After each op the harness waits until every job runs no step, waits at a gate, waits for resources or a decision, or has finished. Expect: outcomes {job: {outcome, error}}; lines {job: [what was published about it, in order]}: 'changed <state> <progress.step>' (+ ' progress <currentFraction in percent>' when the step reported some, ' blockedBy <code>', ' decision <id>'), 'step <kind> <state>', 'log <code>', 'finished <outcome>' (+ ' <error code>'); queueLines ['<queue>: <jobs>' for every queueChanged]; steps {job: ['<kind> <state>' stored, by seq]}; records {job: {state, outcome, plan, mode, libraryId}}; logFile {job: [codes in jobs/<id>/log.jsonl]}; outputs {job: {kind: data}} (stored step outputs); events (every published event, EngineEvent.json, for the cases that list them). finishing {job: '<outcome> <error code>' the Release at the end saw, or null when none ran}. A job's done rows may give readErrors (their StepOutput's) and checkpoint (the row's), and a state other than succeeded. Expect also: checkpoints {job: {kind: the stored row's checkpoint}}; readErrors {job: {kind: the stored output's read errors}}. Crash points (the scenario runners' kill, rearchitecture plan §26; the real roots pass no hook): the runner calls its crash hook on the executor with beforeStep:<kind> before the step asks for its resources (nothing of the step is stored yet) and afterStep:<kind> once the step's finished row is stored (before stepFinished); the Release at the end of a job calls none. What the hook throws stops the runner as a shutdown does, without cancelling anything: nothing more is stored for any job (no step row, record, log or jobFinished) and the run ends with server.stopping. Given crashAt: the point where the harness's hook throws. Expect crashPoints: every point the hook heard, in order; stopped: the jobs whose run ended with server.stopping. Counts (owner H3a-3): every job the runner publishes (jobChanged, jobFinished) once its log is read carries counts {files: the files it produced (the Seal output's files, else the names the Acquire output made: titles' files, others, backup, disc info), warnings and errors: the log lines of that severity (an earlier run's too), readErrors: the read errors of its steps' outputs (stored ones too)}. A log entry (a step's log, a job's given log) is a code (info) or {code, severity}. Expect counts {job: the counts of the last jobChanged or jobFinished published about it}.

expect.rule: a resumed job goes on after a skipped step too, not one step early (recovery resumes jobs; plan §12.3)
the lines recovery (or an earlier run) wrote stay in log.jsonl
the step hasn't ended: this is what a kill would leave
